messages:
maria.g: noticing a sudden throughput drop across a shard in prod-us-west-2, correlates with repeated worker restarts and a handful of GPU OOMs. stack: runtime v2.6.1, kernel-autoswitch enabled.
aj: I see the same on the dashboard — per-second completed requests down ~42% starting ~07:12 UTC. logs show kvcache eviction spikes and kernel fallback churn.
devon: pasted a short excerpt from the worker logs: ```
[07:12:34] WARNING: Kernel mismatch, falling back to generic_kernel_v1
[07:12:34] ERROR: cudaOutOfMemory at alloc_slab(128MB)
[07:12:35] INFO: kvcache: evicted 24 pages, freed 192MB
[07:12:36] INFO: worker respawn (exit code 137)
```
maria.g: interesting — kernel autoswitch seems to be oscillating between optimized kernels -> fallback -> optimized, causing fragmentation and small alloc patterns. KV cache eviction followed immediately by spike in allocations.
tim: added perf profile from the affected worker (saved to s3://redwood-perf/1769998888/profile.pb). high level: a lot of tiny cudaMallocs after fallback, and fragmented free lists.
nikita: batching heuristic telemetry shows request sizes shifted to small groups ~1-3 tokens which reduces packing efficiency — combined with frequent kernel switches that disable some batching fastpaths.
aj: root cause hypothesis: recent kernel selection heuristic change (rollout 7:00 UTC) triggers aggressive autoswitch on small latency regressions; on multi-tenant noisy node this caused repeated kernel churn, which amplified fragmentation and OOMs.
sre-oncall: immediate mitigations? suggestions: 1) pin kernel to stable for prod-us-west-2 pools, 2) increase kvcache slab reservation to avoid cascade eviction, 3) force batcher to prefer slightly larger micro-batches for 10m window.
maria.g: doing 1 & 2 now — rolling a config patch to disable kernel-autoswitch for the pool and bump kvcache_reserved from 1GB -> 2GB. will also open firewall for autoscaling to add 2 more workers as short-term capacity.
deploy-bot: rollout started: config/disable-kernel-autoswitch -> prod-us-west-2 (target 12 nodes) by maria.g at 07:33 UTC.
aj: after the kernel pin and kv bump, initial metrics show worker restarts stopped and eviction rate falling. throughput recovering but still ~10% behind baseline — likely need batching heuristic tweak and a postmortem to adjust the autoswitch thresholds.
devon: can we reproduce locally? I have a repro harness that simulates noisy tenant small-batch surge and kernel fallback path. I'll run with the patched kernel selection to validate.
tim: quick follow-up: save the profiling traces and kvcache stats to the incident folder: s3://incidents/1769998888/ — include slab histograms, free-list churn, and kernel switch events.
nikita: action items: (a) revert kernel-autoswitch rollout and adjust stability window + hysteresis, (b) update batching heuristic to bias grouping for low-latency paths when kernel variance detected, (c) consider increasing minimum slab granularity to reduce fragmentation in presence of churn.
maria.g: assigning: devon -> reproduce + test, aj -> rollback rollout and perf delta analysis, nikita -> batching heuristic draft, tim -> postmortem draft and upload traces. will run a follow-up sync in 45m. :thumbsup:
aj: noting customer-facing impact: one large tenant saw retries spike; CS notified.
sre-oncall: monitoring — will keep alerts muted for noisy restart flaps after config fixes to avoid alert storms. marking incident as "mitigated" pending postmortem.
